default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t1-p1.vietnamese:
Thank you very much for your continued support and patronage.

Our company is conducting a survey to improve our operations and increase customer satisfaction.

Based on the opinions of customers who have contacted our customer service team with questions, we will work to provide even better service.

We kindly ask you to write your opinions in the questions on the “Kameda Customer Satisfaction Survey” we sent you and return it to us.

We apologize for asking this while you are very busy, but we would greatly appreciate your cooperation.

Customers who do not wish to receive emails like this in the future are also kindly asked to let us know.

Kameda Co., Ltd. — Okada, Customer Service Team

Even when someone asks, "Have you been too busy to email me lately?", it is difficult to use the word "busy" once we think about what it means.

default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t11-p1.vietnamese:
Every summer, I hear stories about people in other countries having summer vacations lasting four to six weeks.

Moreover, I feel that the first time I heard about this was not just a few years ago but several decades ago.

Even so, whenever most Japanese people hear about those who have obtained the benefit of long vacations, they exclaim, "How envious!"

Japan is a democratic country.

If most citizens truly wanted this, the country should already have become that way.

If citizens clearly express their desire to build such a country, both politicians and the administrative system will surely act to make it a reality.

default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t12-p1.vietnamese:
It seems that people’s desire to study is growing stronger.

Many people attend classes not only to obtain qualifications or pursue hobbies; there are also many distance-learning courses that allow people to study at home whenever they like.

However, although distance learning is flexible, it is also very difficult to carry out at home.

Many people cannot secure a quiet space because of temptations such as television or alcohol, or because their spouses and children are at home.

So why not open a “Study Club” where people can study before going home?

A “Study Club” is a service that provides a self-study room in the local area in the evening for people taking distance-learning courses.

Recently, we often see foods such as vegetables and meat displayed together with a portrait of the producer and information about how they were produced.

default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t16-p1.vietnamese:
November 20, Heisei 20 (2008)

General Affairs Department, Yutaka Kawaharada

Request for Thorough Energy Conservation in the Office

As winter truly sets in, heating costs (fuel and electricity expenses) are rising sharply.

We are making every effort to implement the following energy-saving measures and ask for everyone’s continued cooperation.

1. Set the room temperature to 20°C when the heater is on.

(If you feel cold, adjust your own temperature by wearing a sweater or cardigan.)

2. Turn off lights in areas that are not being used.

3. When going out or leaving your desk for an extended period, turn off your computer.

4. When leaving work, make sure not to leave printers, personal computers, air conditioners, and so on turned on.

5. During lunch break, turn off lights whenever possible.

default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t17-p1.vietnamese:
Students often tell me, “I don’t want to study grammar or kanji; I want to start with conversation.”

I find this especially difficult to respond to when the students saying this have only just learned the writing system.

People who work for Japanese companies or study Japanese for travel usually want to be able to speak Japanese as soon as possible, rather than study grammar or complicated kanji.

They say they do not need to write emails in Japanese or read Japanese materials, so they want to enroll in a conversation class at all costs.

However, it is difficult to become a good speaker without studying grammar and vocabulary.

Language skills consist of four functions: speaking, listening, writing, and reading. These four functions improve together.

Of course, there may be slight differences depending on the person or on which skill they focus on, but learning a language requires studying all four skills at the same time.

Some students also say that although they have never systematically studied basic Japanese, watching anime or Japanese television dramas has enabled them to understand spoken Japanese naturally and communicate.

However, this approach takes quite a long time before one can understand spoken Japanese, and there are many cases in which people can speak well but cannot even read simple kanji.

In that case, it is difficult to say that they “know Japanese.”

It may be difficult at first, but as you gradually write, read, and listen, you will eventually be able to speak. Therefore, I think you should not rush; study seriously from the basics.

default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t18-p1.vietnamese:
Recently in Japan, enzyme-based weight loss has frequently been covered by television and other media and has become a hot topic.

In particular, because celebrities and models have used this method to lose weight, it has attracted attention mainly among young women.

Although people know that enzymes are beneficial to health and beauty, many are probably surprised that they do not know exactly what enzymes do.

Enzymes help digest food and play important roles in various bodily functions, including metabolism and blood circulation.

The food we eat every day, often without thinking about it, cannot be converted into energy for the body without enzymes.

Because enzymes play an important role in breaking down and absorbing food and nutrients, enzyme-based weight loss is said to improve metabolism, improve the intestinal environment, and reduce body weight.

However, many people who try enzyme-based weight loss apparently do not become thinner; instead, they gain weight. I think this is because they misunderstand the method.

If people eat more than their daily food intake because they think they are supplementing their enzymes, or drink excessive amounts of enzyme beverages because they believe that simply drinking them will make them lose weight, they may gain weight.

This is because enzymes do not make the calories consumed disappear, and many enzyme beverages contain sweeteners or syrup to make them easier to drink.

To avoid such mistakes and misunderstandings, we must first consider what enzymes do and why they are necessary.

I believe that understanding these points before starting enzyme-based weight loss can lead to better results.

default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t19-p1.vietnamese:
When I was young, I loved playing outdoors.

In particular, during the summer and winter vacations, I often went to a small stream to catch fish with a net or went into the mountains to gather firewood.

I had many siblings and relatives. On ordinary days, I stayed at home, but whenever the summer or winter vacation came around, I would go to my aunt and uncle’s house and play to my heart’s content with my cousins.

Sometimes, we used branches we had gathered in the mountains to build our own secret base.

Other times, we made fake money out of paper and played shop.

We even crumpled newspaper into balls to play baseball, and used a rice paddle to play table tennis.

Everything around us became material for play. We never grew tired of playing, and we came up with ideas together about what to play and how to play it.

Back then, my face was dark from the sun. My hair was always cut short like a boy’s, and I never wore dresses.

When I entered middle school and my personality began to mellow a little, I noticed that my skin was getting whiter and whiter. Worried that I might have some illness, I seriously asked my mother about it.

Laughing, my mother said, “That’s because you used to play outside all the time.”

Whenever I look back on my childhood, I feel even more deeply that I really was an extremely energetic child.

However, when I look at children today, I feel that they are completely different from what I was like as a child.

Although they are only elementary school students, they have no time to play because of their studies. And even when they do play, most of the time each child is absorbed in playing alone on a phone or video game console.

For some reason, seeing things like that makes me feel rather sad.

Of course, times change, and each era has its own trends. Even so, I still think the days when everyone exercised together and searched for materials to play with using their own hands were much more fun.

default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t2-p1.vietnamese:
Recently, we often hear news about people being forced to resign, developing depression, or even committing suicide because of workplace power harassment (pawa-hara).

“Pawa-hara” is short for “power harassment.” It refers to using one’s position or authority to cause excessive mental or physical suffering to someone working in the same organization.

One common form is verbal abuse. This includes hurling insulting remarks such as “Drop dead” or “You’re a wage thief,” as well as shouting and scolding.

Another common form is physical abuse, such as punching, slapping, or throwing objects at someone.

In addition to these forms of harassment, isolating someone from workplace relationships, assigning work that is far too difficult, or conversely making someone do nothing but simple tasks such as photocopying and cleaning are also forms of pawa-hara.

(※) 怒鳴る (Donaru): To call out in a very loud voice; to shout angrily or scold loudly.

default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t20-p1.vietnamese:
Recently, someone told me, “It is best not to use email. Even if it is short, calling is better. Feelings can be conveyed through the tone of one's voice.”

I feel that the problem is not that email fails to convey feelings, but that it conveys them too strongly.

In particular, the persuasive power created by sentences that combine words cannot be weak.

If we think about how many people have been moved by books made up solely of written words, we can understand the magnitude of that influence.

The feelings hidden behind the good intention of encouraging someone may reveal themselves in the wording.

Without being conscious of it at all, those feelings may accidentally appear in the words in the form of 'Compared with that person, I am very happy.'

Precisely because, unlike with a phone call, we cannot immediately see the other person's reaction, we may continue writing without realizing what our words convey.

When unsure whether it is all right to send an email, it may be better to think that we cannot write an email to encourage someone.

default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t21-p1.vietnamese:
It is best not to borrow money if possible, but the important point here is that "once you have borrowed money, you should repay it as soon as possible." It is often difficult for the lender to say, "Please pay me back."

However, borrowing a large sum of money not only damages relationships between people; in many cases, the money ultimately is not returned. Therefore, it is better to think, "If you lend money, do so prepared to give it away."

The same applies when someone treats you to a meal or gives you a gift. Whatever the situation, you should return the favor in some way. There are many ways to do so.

For example, you could give the other person a CD or book they once wanted, or provide information that they would probably appreciate.

It does not have to be an expensive gift. If you put your whole heart into doing "something useful for the other person," what you do with the intention of returning the favor may instead be met with the other person's gratitude and appreciation.

What matters is the feeling of "wanting to return the favor," and by acting on that feeling, you will surely receive something even greater in return.

default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t22-p1.vietnamese:
① “People who wait for instructions” refers to people who “do not act unless they are told to” and “can do only exactly what they are instructed to do.”

When asking such a person to do something, you need to be extremely careful if, even after replying “yes,” they do not ask any questions about the task.

The major characteristics of a “person who waits for instructions” are that, regarding assigned tasks, they ask no questions, seek no confirmation, and provide no progress reports along the way.

Among subordinates like this, many often say things such as, “No one told me to do it, so I didn’t,” or “I wasn’t told.”

If we do not give them instructions about this or that, they do not move at all. ② When giving instructions to a subordinate who waits for instructions, it is important to make sure they clearly understand the purpose of the task.

By clearly communicating the purpose, they will gradually develop a certain degree of ability to respond flexibly.

For example, when asking them to photocopy materials for a meeting, explain carefully what kind of meeting it is, what time the materials will be used, who will attend, and how many people will participate.

As a result, they will gradually figure out for themselves, “What form should I prepare this in?”

default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t23-p1.outline.0.note: A common problem is that daily contact makes it easy to notice other people's flaws; frustration with someone incompatible can make oneself negative as well.
default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t23-p1.outline.1.label: Advice: look back on yourself objectively.
default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t23-p1.outline.1.note: The author advises looking at oneself objectively because people do not understand themselves as well as they think; before becoming dissatisfied with others, one should reconsider one’s own actions and words. Evidence for Questions 1 and 2.

default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t23-p1.outline.2.note: Considers the possibility that the author themselves may be the strange one in their colleagues’ eyes, conveying the main message that one should change one’s perspective and calmly examine oneself. Question 3 is based here.
default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t23-p1.vietnamese:
When you see someone every day, you will inevitably notice their flaws, even if you do not want to.

Have you ever had an experience like this?

No matter how cheerfully you greet the other person, they do not respond right away.

Sometimes, when they start a conversation with you, it turns out to be nothing but pointless talk.

Because there are people you do not get along with, you may feel that you yourself are gradually becoming unpleasant, and feel unbearably frustrated.

At times like these, try looking at yourself objectively.

Although we may assume that we understand ourselves better than anyone else, in reality, we do not understand ourselves as well as we think.

Before holding a grudge against or feeling dissatisfied with the other person, try thinking once more, and more deeply, about your own actions and words.

Even if you think you are doing your best, it is possible that your efforts are only one-sided.

Sometimes, the person everyone at work calls “strange” or “different” may actually be you.

I think it is good to occasionally change the way we see ourselves and calmly take another look at who we are.

default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t24-p1.vietnamese:
The other person's resistant attitude is simply because communication has not been going smoothly; there is no other reason.

Think for yourself about whether there has been too little dialogue in your daily interactions, or whether you have failed to communicate what needed to be communicated.

When relationships between people are good, problems can normally be resolved properly through discussion and exchange.

However, once a relationship has deteriorated, it cannot immediately become good again.

Therefore, let us stop making unnecessary comments and criticisms along the way.

In other words, give only the “initial instructions” and “the result you want,” and try not to say anything beyond what is necessary.

When the other person achieves a good result, praise and acknowledge them.

By doing this, the other person will surely gradually open up to you as well.

In addition, an open workplace with a positive atmosphere is also an important key point.

People with resistant attitudes often act according to their emotions, so if you know how to bring out their abilities skillfully, they will work hard to move things forward and may ultimately become your strongest partners.

default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t25-p1.vietnamese:
“My child refuses to go to bed early in the evening.”

“I feel that my child gets too little sleep. Is their health all right?!”

…These are complaints often heard from working mothers (①).

Even on busy days, children staying up until late at night is fairly common, partly because mothers want to spend as much time with their children as possible.

However, for young children, sleep is just as important as meals.

Doctors say that “sleeping, eating, and bathing” are the most important things for young children’s development.

Recently, some children stay up until 11 or 12 at night, but children should be put to bed before 9 p.m.

Besides, does not the mother also want some time for herself?

Playing with one’s child is certainly fun, but if the child stays awake forever, the mother cannot read her favorite book, watch television, or do the housework, which is very troublesome.

What can be done so that ② the child can go to bed early?

default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t26-p1.vietnamese:
7:30　I left home a little earlier than usual.

8:00　I entered a room inside a building.

I put my bag in a locker, took the box with my name on it, and stood in front of a cooking station.

That's right. This was a cooking class for men that opened early in the morning.

I opened the lid of the box and checked today's recipe and ingredients.

This was not a class where a teacher constantly stayed with us and gave instructions. It was a cooking class in which we followed the recipe on our own.

We could ask the teacher about anything we did not understand.

(15-minute breakfast, 10-minute packed lunch...) Since it was before work, there was not much time to spare, but paying attention to the time while cooking increased my serious concentration, and my skills also... improved more quickly.

In addition, this class was very popular because its program involved making and eating one's own breakfast, as well as making a packed lunch.

8:45　Although I ran a little over time, somehow I managed to finish.

After eating breakfast and cleaning up, I left the class at 9:05.

Because it was near my company, I arrived at work 10 minutes before starting time today as well.

default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t27-p1.outline.1.label: The origin of the name Castella
default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t27-p1.outline.1.note: The passage presents two theories about the name’s origin: it may come from the Portuguese pronunciation of Castilla, a place in Spain, or from the phrase “rise high like a castle (castelo)” shouted while whipping egg whites.
default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t27-p1.outline.2.label: Characteristics and traditional method of making Castella
default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t27-p1.outline.2.note: Shifts to the characteristics of old-fashioned Castella: it used only three ingredients—flour, sugar, and eggs—in equal proportions, and was baked in a steam-baking pot from below. This supports Question 3.
default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t27-p1.outline.3.label: The Japanization process and Japanese creativity
default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t27-p1.outline.3.note: Describes the improvement process beginning in the Meiji period, when malt produced a soft, moist, airy cake that became wagashi. Praises the Japanese spirit of creativity, adopting foreign culture and elevating it into something uniquely Japanese. Evidence for Questions 1 and 2.
default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t27-p1.vietnamese:
When you hear the word Castella, what comes to mind first? You probably immediately think of Nagasaki.

Nagasaki Prefecture lies in the western part of Kyushu and was the only place where Japan maintained contact with foreign countries throughout the period of national seclusion.

Because many Dutch and Chinese people came and went through Nagasaki, it was once a city where information from abroad arrived in abundance.

Castella cake, widely known as a specialty of Nagasaki, was introduced by the Portuguese during this period, and there are many theories about the origin of its name.

The usual theory is that the name derives from "castela," the Portuguese pronunciation of Castilla, a region in Spain.

Another theory holds that, during the production of Castella, when the whipped egg whites, or meringue, rose high, people shouted, "Rise high like a castle (castelo)!" and that the name of the cake originated from this phrase.

However, it is said that Castella at that time was very different from the Castella of today.

The ingredients used for Castella at that time consisted of only three things: flour, sugar, and eggs, all mixed in equal proportions.

The method apparently involved mixing the ingredients thoroughly, placing them in a baking pot, covering it tightly, and cooking it with heat from below.

Later, over the course of time, the proportions of the ingredients and the sweeteners used gradually changed.

Castella became as moist, soft, and finely textured as it is today from the Meiji period onward, as Japanese pastry artisans continually adapted it to suit Japanese tastes.

In addition to sugar, they also began using malt syrup, which suited Japanese preferences. Improvements in the preparation method created the uniquely moist and soft Castella associated with Japan.

In short, although Castella was introduced from abroad, it was transformed and refined into a unique cake of Japan, which is why it is now considered a traditional Japanese confection (Wagashi).

This demonstrates the remarkable quality of the Japanese: rather than merely accepting imported things exactly as they were, they continually explore and innovate, reshaping them into things with a strong identity of their own.

default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t28-p1.vietnamese:
Because of the prolonged economic downturn, the unemployment rate in South Korea is continuing to rise.

Among other groups, youth unemployment in particular has become a serious problem.

In the past, many people may have thought that having a high level of education would open the way to a brighter, more prosperous future and allow them to live a rosy life.

However, in today’s society, even with a high level of education and a well-developed résumé, finding a job is becoming increasingly difficult, causing feelings of anxiety and stress to grow as well.

University education tends to become preparation for job applications rather than a means of deepening knowledge, and universities are no longer places devoted purely to academic study.

Furthermore, even when young people find jobs, they are not hired as regular employees but as non-regular workers, forcing them to live in hardship or with constant anxiety about the future.

Although the work performed by non-regular workers is not very different from that of regular employees, they are disadvantaged in many ways: they have no opportunities for promotion, their hourly wages do not increase, and they do not receive bonuses.

Therefore, regardless of their abilities, young people seeking stable lives look for positions where their futures are guaranteed to some extent rather than joining ordinary companies.

This is why competition for the civil service examination held annually in South Korea has grown so intense, and it also reflects the country’s unfortunate reality.

The fact that young people—who are expected to shine in various fields—are not participating in economic activities but are instead devoting their energy to civil service examinations is a loss for the country.

To solve a problem like this, I believe national-level measures and a change in public awareness are necessary.

Some major companies have experimented with removing the résumé section asking applicants to list their credentials and prioritizing each person’s experience, but this alone cannot become a fundamental solution.

A new recruitment system that values applicants’ individual abilities, personalities, and qualities must be established, along with a suitable environment.

In addition, expanding financial support so that young people can search for jobs adequately is essential.

The longer the job search lasts, the greater the financial burden becomes, so providing assistance and support for them is also very important.

Helping capable young South Koreans fully demonstrate their strengths in their respective fields is probably an urgent task today.

default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t29-p1.outline.0.note: Begins by noting that everyone prefers days off and often feels down at the beginning of the week, and advises accepting this as natural in order to find ways to improve it.
default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t29-p1.outline.1.label: Solution 1: adjusting the weekend schedule
default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t29-p1.outline.1.note: Method 1 recommends not cramming too many plans into the weekend out of fear of loneliness, and leaving one day flexible according to one's physical condition.
default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t29-p1.outline.2.label: Solution 2: get up early and take action to build motivation
default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t29-p1.outline.2.note: Solution 2 recommends getting up early on Monday morning because action creates motivation and helps one prepare mentally and stay alert before going to work.
default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t29-p1.vietnamese:
“Tomorrow is Monday. I can’t wait to go to work.” — Isn’t it quite rare to find someone looking forward to it so eagerly?

Who doesn’t think a day off is better than work?

When they think about their vacation ending and having to work all week again, quite a few people feel depressed and physically unwell.

Rather than thinking you are the only useless, unmotivated person, consider feeling down at the beginning of the week ①natural, and think about how you can start feeling better.

【Remedy 1】

Stop filling ②Saturday and Sunday with so many plans that you have no time to let your body rest.

If you pack your schedule completely because you think having no plans would be lonely, you will have no time to rest at all, so it is only natural that you become tired.

Moreover, if those plans do not go as expected, they will become a major source of stress.

Have you ever felt regretful, thinking, “I accidentally slept until well past noon and wasted my precious day off”?

③At times like this, even though your body is actually getting some rest, your mood still sinks.

Over the two days of Saturday and Sunday, make your plans so that you have one day when you can act according to how you feel physically and emotionally that day.

【Remedy 2】

Get up a little earlier on Monday morning.

Keep in mind that action comes first and motivation follows; for now, just get out of bed.

Motivation is not something you can create simply by wanting to. It arises naturally as you take action.

Your company is not paying you for your enthusiasm; it is paying you for the specific amount of work you actually accomplish.

By the time you leave the house, make sure your mind is completely awake and ready.

default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t3-p1.vietnamese:
Recently, cosmetics for men have been increasing, and products such as foundation for men are now commonly seen in pharmacies.

Not only entertainers but also ordinary office workers and university students wear makeup to make their skin look better.

When women aged 20 to 60 were asked, “Do you think it is acceptable for men to wear makeup?”, about half answered, “Yes.”

Moreover, when the results were examined by age group, the percentage of people who thought it was acceptable for men to wear makeup exceeded half among the younger groups: 62.3% among those in their 20s and 51.3% among those in their 30s.

By contrast, only 30% of women in their 60s answered, “Yes,” suggesting that there is still some reluctance toward men wearing makeup.

For men, however, makeup does not mean applying mascara, eyeliner, or lipstick as women do. Its main purpose is skincare, making the skin look better, so I do not think there is any reason to criticize it.

default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t30-p1.vietnamese:
About 5 km from my company, a new restaurant has opened.

The road there has always been known for heavy traffic and congestion.

One day, while walking along the sidewalk, I realized that the restaurant had opened sometime earlier, so I decided to stop in for lunch.

The restaurant serves only lunch, with just three choices: A, B, and C.

I therefore chose Lunch B, which was in the middle price range: 950 yen, including dessert and a drink.

When the meal arrived, I began eating out of habit at my usual speed and finished very quickly.

The dish may have been delicious, but by the time I realized it, it was too late. Habit is truly frightening; the time I could have spent savoring the flavor had passed in the blink of an eye.

As you know, the pleasure obtained from food is always proportional to both its deliciousness and the time spent enjoying it.

Just as I was finishing the main dish, a young chef wearing a tall white hat came over and asked, “How was your meal?” ① Oh no. I realized that this chef was genuinely serious and passionate about his work, while I had not tasted the food carefully enough to offer a proper impression.

It is not unusual for a chef to visit each table and talk with the customers after a meal, but I wondered why he had come out for a single meal such as Lunch B.

Through my conversation with the chef, I learned that both the soup and the main dish were new experiments of his.

As you know, ② the deliciousness of a dish is proportional to the chef’s passion.

default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t31-p1.vietnamese:
When you become part of the working world, communicating and getting along with people you do not click with also becomes part of your job.

Since we work to earn a salary, it is impossible to have only friends we like around us and spend our time working while laughing and having fun.

“Before we know it, we find ourselves placed in human relationships we cannot choose for ourselves”—① that is what a company is.

However, “overcoming our reluctance and learning to get along with others helps us grow a little as human beings.” ② Try to think positively in this way and keep your emotions under control.

【③ Problems caused by feelings of reluctance and aversion】

When there is someone you dislike, have you ever thought, “Ugh, I hate them,” or “I really do not want to see them,” and then spent the entire day thinking about that person?

If you keep thinking only about someone you dislike, you are wasting your own precious time.

When relationships with others do not go smoothly, people often unconsciously fall into a depressed, gloomy mood.

Naturally, work becomes less enjoyable, and your motivation to work disappears as well.

In other words, you will be unable to make full use of your abilities.

When dealing with someone you dislike, it is easy to become emotional, irritated, or uncomfortable.

When these feelings continue to build and you can no longer control them, you may even want to quit your job.

【For those who still feel, “No matter what, someone I dislike is still someone I dislike”】

No matter how much you think and worry about the situation, accept that the other person is not going to change.

At times like that, it is important to forgive them and generously let things go, seeing them as “someone who can only express themselves in that way.”

Holding on to unforgiveness toward someone you hate only causes you more suffering.

Wouldn’t it be a terrible waste to grow old while worrying so much about relationships with others?

It is best to develop your own way of changing your mood and work cheerfully.

default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t32-p1.outline.0.label: The nature of vitality and future direction
default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t32-p1.outline.0.note: Raises the issue of Japanese people lacking vitality despite their wealth, comparing them with older people in the United States who look toward the future, and asserts that vitality comes from knowing what one is moving toward.
default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t32-p1.outline.1.label: Lessons from energetic business managers
default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t32-p1.outline.1.note: Relates this to how successful business leaders make use of human resources by encouraging employees to take the initiative in finding work they want to do.
default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t32-p1.outline.2.label: Two conditions for making personal identity concrete
default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t32-p1.outline.2.note: Presents two essential factors: discovering what one truly wants to do and having absolute confidence that it will become reality.
default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t32-p1.outline.3.label: The concluding message about the joy of moving forward
default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t32-p1.outline.3.note: The author asserts that as long as people grasp the direction and feel they are moving closer to their goal, anyone can find joy and vitality.
default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t32-p1.vietnamese:
Recently, people often say that Japanese people in general are losing their vitality.

The fact that Japanese people—who should be wealthy both as a nation and as individuals—lack vitality proves that wealth itself is not the source of vitality.

It is said that in the United States, people in their forties and fifties enthusiastically attend university as students even without much money.

Perhaps this is because they believe in themselves and in the future ahead.

The issue is not what position a person currently occupies. What shows whether someone is discouraged or has regained vitality is whether they can feel and understand where they are heading.

In times like these, the thoughts of energetic, passionate business leaders are well worth considering.

Listening to such people, I feel that in a country like Japan, which has few natural resources, they are making effective use of a resource called “people.”

It could be said that they follow a basic rule: instead of waiting for someone else to tell them what to do, finding what needs to be done and taking action themselves allows them to bring out many times more strength.

I think two things are needed in order to give concrete form to the individuality one has discovered within oneself.

1. Find what you truly want to do.

2. Believe without the slightest doubt that it will become a reality.

Even if you have not yet found the first thing in concrete terms, simply understanding the general direction will surely lead you to discover something that interests you.

No matter what position you are in, being able to feel and understand that you are moving closer to that destination is surely a source of joy for anyone.

default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t34-p1.vietnamese:
The Tokyo Art Center’s collection exhibition, 「An Invitation to Distant Memories」, was held from September 23 to October 22, 2017.

This exhibition introduced how people in the Edo period interacted with nature and lived their lives through contemporary watercolor paintings.

In particular, through works centered on nature, visitors could sense how people faced and connected with nature in their daily lives during each season.

Through spring flowers, the green of summer, falling leaves in autumn, and winter snow scenes, visitors could reflect on the appeal of the four seasons and the mutually supportive relationship between people and nature.

The opening hours were from 9:00 to 17:00, with extended hours until 18:00 on Saturdays and Sundays. The regular closing day was Monday each week; however, the center remained open when Monday fell on a public holiday.

Admission was 1,200 yen for adults and 800 yen for students from junior high school through university. Elementary school students and younger children, as well as people aged 60 or older, were admitted free of charge. Groups of 15 or more received a 200-yen discount from the applicable regular price.

Audio guides were available in English and Chinese. Visitors needed to show identification or pay a 200-yen deposit.

default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t39-p1.vietnamese:
Are you lying in bed playing with your phone before going to sleep while worrying that you may have insomnia?

It is not only looking at your phone for hours in a completely dark room with the lights off that can cause problems. Even if you keep looking at your phone for a while because you cannot sleep, you may genuinely develop insomnia. Simply checking your email briefly or looking at the news can significantly interfere with sleep. This is because if new information is sent to the brain before bedtime, the brain wakes up and begins to function. Even if you intend to go to sleep, you will probably be unable to do so if your mind keeps racing. In addition, the LED lights used to illuminate smartphone screens disrupt your sleep rhythm. The blue light emitted by LEDs closely resembles morning light, which wakes the brain, so exposure to it before bedtime not only makes it difficult to sleep but instead leaves the brain alert and awake.

default.p.4nd_dokkai_n3-t4-p1.vietnamese:
"Self-esteem" is how a person feels about themselves.

When someone positively evaluates themselves by thinking, "I have value," their self-esteem is considered high; when they negatively evaluate themselves by thinking, "I am useless," their self-esteem is considered low.

In its true sense, "high self-esteem" means thinking, "I am fine as I am." Even if one is not perfect, one can still feel that one is okay and does not need to be superior to others.

No matter what one is like, it is important to be able to think, "I have value."

This kind of self-esteem, meaning the ability to accept oneself as one is, is sometimes also called "self-acceptance."

Did Japanese people in the past dislike war and resist it?

Since images of citizens supporting the war can be seen in many places, it is difficult to say for certain that they did.

Women also cooperated with the war in various ways.

The National Defense Women's Association, which was responsible for encouraging soldiers, had more than 10 million members. This shows that women were also a presence that could not be overlooked during the war.

Furthermore, the mass media, which was very familiar to ordinary citizens, enthusiastically praised the war.

I was serving on the management committee of the apartment complex where I live when, at the residents’ general meeting the other day, a proposal was made by parents of elementary school students.

“Because we teach the children to run away whenever a stranger greets them, we would like a rule prohibiting residents from greeting one another in the complex.”

Children cannot distinguish between residents and nonresidents, and the parents also said that this made educating them difficult.

Then some older residents expressed their views: “It is very irritating when you greet someone and they do not respond. In that case, let us both stop greeting one another.” Everyone eventually agreed.

default.q.4nd_dokkai_n3-t1-q1.explanation: The key N3 grammar pattern is 「N + を基にして」, meaning “based on N” or “using N as the foundation,” and commonly used formally in written language and business correspondence: 「当社のサービスチームへお問い合わせいただいたお客様の意見を基にして、より良いサービスをご提供できるように努力して参ります。」 (“Based on the opinions of customers who contacted our service team, we will strive to provide even better service.”) The survey group is specifically limited to customers who had submitted inquiries (お問い合わせいただいたお客様), so choice (b), which claims 「アンケート調査には誰でも参加できる」, directly contradicts the passage. Learners may confuse this with (a), but the final sentence, 「これからこのようなメールを受信されたくない方もご返信お願いいたします」, shows that people who do not wish to receive similar emails in the future must also reply, so (a) matches the text. For questions asking which statement is inconsistent, watch for extreme generalizations such as 「誰でも」 (“anyone”), which often exaggerate the scope of the original information.

default.q.4nd_dokkai_n3-t10-q1.explanation: The key grammar patterns in the question and answer are N + からすると, which follows a noun referring to a person and indicates a viewpoint (“from the standpoint or perspective of...” ), and V-る / Nの + おそれがある, which expresses concern about a possible negative risk. Accordingly, the complete meaning of correct choice (a) is: “From the other person’s perspective, there is a risk that it may be understood to mean that they are not actually that important to the speaker.” The crucial evidence is the original sentence:「これはつまり、「あなたは自分にとってそれほど大事な人ではない。」という意味にも取れます。」It clearly explains that saying one is busy can imply that the other person is not important enough to make time for. To avoid the trap in choice (b), carefully distinguish the degree-negation pattern それほど〜ない (“not to that extent”) from the superlative comparison pattern 〜ほど…はない (“there is no one or nothing as...”). Focusing only on the particle ほど while overlooking the ending can easily lead to the completely opposite interpretation.

The author argues that Japan is a democratic country, so the political and administrative systems should respond when citizens actively speak up and clearly express their wishes in order to make a long holiday possible.
default.q.4nd_dokkai_n3-t11-q1.explanation: The key evidence reflecting the author's complete viewpoint appears in the conclusion: 「国民がそうしたい国にしたいという意思表示をすれば、それを可能にするために政治も行政も動くはずです。」 (If citizens clearly express their desire to make the country that way, both politics and public administration should certainly act to make it possible.) Grammatically, the author combines the conditional form 「〜ば」, indicating a necessary condition, with 「V plain form + はずだ」, which expresses a well-founded inference or expectation meaning “should certainly / is expected to...”. The key noun is 「意思表示」 (“an expression of one's will; clearly stating one's position”). The argument criticizes the passive attitude of people who merely envy other countries (「うらやましい」) and emphasizes that in a democracy, policy changes occur only when citizens actively speak up. A common trap is choice (c), which includes 「望む」 (“wish for”), a word found in the passage. However, the author makes clear that merely wishing (望む) produces no result; people must take the additional step of expressing their will (意思表示), as stated in choice (d).

The passage states that turning one’s efforts and experience of improving at swimming into the topic of a personal essay can also improve one’s language arts grade.
default.q.4nd_dokkai_n3-t15-q1.explanation: The decisive evidence is the concluding sentence: 「がんばって泳げるようになったことを、泳ぎの得意な子どもは何メートルも泳げるようになったことを生活作文にすれば、国語の成績までよくなります。」 (“If you write a daily-life composition about the effort it took to learn to swim, or, for children who are good swimmers, about how many meters they have learned to swim, even their Japanese-language grades will improve.”). Grammatically, the author uses the conditional form 「～ば」 (the Group 3 verb する becomes すれば), expressing the hypothetical meaning “if... then...,” together with the particle 「まで」 after 「国語の成績」 to express an unexpected extension: “even their Japanese-language grades.” This emphasizes that recording a swimming experience can provide benefits beyond ordinary physical training. Option (a) is correct because it accurately paraphrases 「泳げるようになった」 as 「泳ぎが上達した」 and uses 「～ようになる」 to indicate a positive change in ability and grades. An important N3 reading-comprehension strategy is not to choose an option merely because it repeats a keyword such as 「体育」 in option (b). The pattern 「～だけに利用してしまうのはもったいない」 (“it would be a waste to use it only for...”) expresses regret and criticism of limiting its purpose to physical education, which is the opposite of the advice 「利用したほうがいい」.

The author finds it difficult to accept that relationships among neighbors have changed so much that people now collectively agree not to greet one another in their own neighborhood.
default.q.4nd_dokkai_n3-t6-q1.explanation: The key phrase 「理解に苦しむ」 (noun + に苦しむ) means “to find something extremely difficult to understand” or “to be unable to make sense of something,” often with a tone of shock, helplessness, or difficulty accepting something contrary to common sense. The strongest evidence is in the final sentence: 「その告知を出すのですが、世の中変わったな、と理解に苦しんでいます。」 (Although I am about to post that notice, I find it very difficult to understand and think, “The world has really changed.”) Through the sigh 「世の中変わったな」, the author expresses distress over how the neighborhood custom of greeting one another warmly, once valued, is now considered bothersome and rejected by both older and younger people. Learners may choose option (d) because of the striking proposal made by an elementary school parent, but the clue is the clause before the quotation particle 「～と」: the changing times (世の中) are the core reason the author finds the situation so difficult to accept.

To improve the relationship, the author stresses that one should first listen to what the other person is saying, leaving judgments about its value or correctness until later.
default.q.4nd_dokkai_n3-t8-q1.explanation: In the reading, the author states the solution for improving relationships in the sentence: 「でも、相手が話しているという今の事実、今の経験は今尊重するしかないのです。その態度が相手と自分の人間関係をよくするのです」(Translation: "However, there is no choice but to respect, right now, the present fact and experience of the other person speaking; that attitude will improve the relationship between the other person and oneself."). Grammatically, 「V-る + しかない」means "there is no choice but to..." and expresses the urgency and necessity of acting immediately in a communication situation. The author also points out that 「価値判断...というのはいつでもできます」(value judgments can be made at any time); therefore, clearly separating the issue and making the judgment later is the core of choice (a). When answering, watch for familiar traps: choice (c) reverses the keyword by changing 「分離する」to the negative 「分離しない」, while choice (d) uses 「〜ながら」(while doing...) in a way that directly conflicts with 「意見を言わずに」(without expressing an opinion while listening).
default.q.4nd_dokkai_n3-t8-q1.why.0: ✓ (a) Correct because the passage states that judgment can be made at any time and should come later; what is urgent is listening to and respecting the truth the other person is telling you.
default.q.4nd_dokkai_n3-t8-q1.why.1: ✗ (b) The author says that one should listen to the facts first, not set them aside in order to express one's own opinion.
default.q.4nd_dokkai_n3-t8-q1.why.2: ✗ (c) Incorrect because the passage states that listening means separating (分離する) the confirmation of facts from value judgments, which is the opposite of "not separating" (分離しない).
default.q.4nd_dokkai_n3-t8-q1.why.3: ✗ (d) Incorrect because the author advocates 「意見を言わずにとにかく聞く」 (“listen without giving opinions”), so one cannot both listen and make value judgments.

According to the researcher, when people are sleeping lightly, their brains remain alert and respond to dreams as if they were reality. As a result, the dreams feel highly realistic—“more real than reality.”
default.q.4nd_dokkai_n3-t9-q1.explanation: The basis is the researcher’s quoted opinion: 「夢は浅い眠りの間に見るもので、その時、体は眠っていても脳は起きていて見る夢に現実と同じように反応しているそうです。そこで見る夢は現実以上の現実だとその研究者は主張していました。」 (Dreams occur during light sleep; although the body is asleep, the brain is awake and responds to dreams as it does to reality. The researcher claimed that dreams seen then are even more real than reality itself.) The key grammar point is `〜と同じように` (used with `N + と同じように` or a verb in the dictionary or ta-form), meaning "just like" or "in the same way as." It compares the manner or qualities of two things. Because the brain receives and responds to the dream as it would to reality, together with the claim that dreams are "more real than reality," answer (a) accurately conveys the highly realistic nature of dreams. Learners should watch for the trap in (c): the question asks for the opinion of the researcher (夢研究者), whereas thinking about pleasant things to make it easier to sleep is the author’s personal experience (「私」), not a scientifically demonstrated conclusion.
default.q.4nd_dokkai_n3-t9-q1.why.0: ✓ (a) This choice is correct because it accurately reflects the researcher's claim that the brain responds to dreams as though they were reality and that dreams possess an exceptionally realistic quality.
default.q.4nd_dokkai_n3-t9-q1.why.1: ✗ (b) This choice contradicts the passage, which clearly states that the brain reacts exactly as it does in real life (「現実と同じように反応している」).
default.q.4nd_dokkai_n3-t9-q1.why.2: ✗ (c) This choice is incorrect because it describes the author's personal experience, not a researcher's opinion. The author also states that imagining things would lead to peaceful sleep.
default.q.4nd_dokkai_n3-t9-q1.why.3: ✗ (d) This is incorrect because the article states that although the body is asleep, the brain remains awake and responds to dreams (「体は眠っていても脳は起きていて…」).
